events: Shaheedi Purab – Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji
title: Shaheedi Purab of Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji: the first Sikh martyr and the chhabeel
desc: In 1606 Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji was tortured to death in Lahore on Jahangir's orders. Why it happened, Gurdwara Dera Sahib, and why Sikhs serve cold water on the day.
cap: Gurdwara Dera Sahib, Lahore, beside the place where Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji was martyred
body: The Shaheedi Purab of Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji remembers the martyrdom of the fifth Sikh Guru in Lahore in 1606. He was the first of the Gurus to give his life, and his shaheedi shaped everything that followed in Sikh history.
## Why the Guru was arrested

By 1606 the Sikh community had grown into a strong and organised body around Sri Harmandir Sahib and the Adi Granth, and the Guru's teaching drew people of every faith. The emperor Jahangir, newly on the throne, wrote in his own memoirs that he had long wished to put an end to the Guru's influence. When his rebel son Khusrau passed through Punjab and was received at the Guru's court, Jahangir had the pretext he needed. The Guru was summoned to Lahore, fined heavily and asked to remove passages from the Granth; he refused both.
## The torture in Lahore

Over several days in the summer heat, the Guru was made to sit on a red-hot iron plate while burning sand was poured over him, and was boiled in a cauldron. Tradition remembers that the Muslim saint Mian Mir, who had laid the foundation stone of Sri Harmandir Sahib, offered to intervene, and the Guru asked him not to, accepting the Divine Will as sweet. He was then taken to the river Ravi, where his body disappeared into the water. Gurdwara Dera Sahib now stands at the place, beside the Lahore Fort.
## The chhabeel

Because the Guru was tortured in the burning heat of summer, Sikhs mark the day by setting up chhabeels along roads and outside gurdwaras, serving cold sweetened water and milk to every passer-by, whatever their faith. Gurdwaras hold Akhand Paath and kirtan, and many sangats recite Sukhmani Sahib, the Guru's own bani of peace.

events: Shaheedi Purab – Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji
title: Shaheedi Purab of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji: Hind di Chadar
desc: In 1675 Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji gave his life at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, for the freedom of others to follow their faith. The story of Hind di Chadar and the day.
alt: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi
cap: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Chandni Chowk, where Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji was martyred
body: The Shaheedi Purab of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji remembers the martyrdom of the ninth Sikh Guru at Chandni Chowk in Delhi in November 1675. He gave his life not for his own faith but for the right of others to practise theirs, and Sikhs remember him as Hind di Chadar, the shield of India.
## The plea of the Kashmiri Pandits

Under the emperor Aurangzeb, the Pandits of Kashmir were being pressed to convert to Islam. A group led by Pandit Kirpa Ram came to the Guru at Anandpur Sahib and asked for his help. The Guru told them to tell the authorities that if Guru Tegh Bahadur could be made to convert, they would all follow. He then set out for Delhi with a few companions and was arrested on the way.
## Chandni Chowk

Held in Delhi, the Guru was given three choices: accept Islam, perform a miracle to prove his holiness, or die. He refused the first two. To break his resolve, his companions Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji and Bhai Dyala Ji were put to death before his eyes. On the day, the Guru was beheaded in the open at Chandni Chowk. In the confusion of a storm, Bhai Jaita Ji carried the Guru's head to Anandpur Sahib, and Bhai Lakhi Shah Vanjara took his body to his house and set the house alight to cremate it.
## How the day is observed

Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib marks the place of the martyrdom, and Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib the place of the cremation. Sangats hold Akhand Paath, kirtan, katha and Nagar Kirtan, and many recite his saloks, which close the reading of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

events: Shaheedi – Bhai Dyala Ji, Bhai Mati Das Ji & Bhai Sati Das Ji
title: Bhai Mati Das, Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Dyala Ji: the three martyrs of Chandni Chowk
desc: Three Sikhs arrested with Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji were put to death before him in Delhi in 1675: sawn, burnt and boiled. Who they were and how they are remembered.
alt: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Old Delhi
cap: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Delhi, near which the three Sikhs were martyred
body: This day remembers three Sikhs who were put to death in Delhi in November 1675, in front of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji, so that the sight of their suffering might break the Guru's resolve. It did not, and neither did theirs.
## Who they were

Bhai Mati Das Ji and Bhai Sati Das Ji were brothers from the village of Kariala, near Jhelum, from a family that had served the Gurus for generations. Bhai Mati Das Ji was the Guru's diwan, his steward, and Bhai Sati Das Ji wrote Persian for the Guru. Bhai Dyala Ji, from Alipur near Multan, was a close companion of the Guru and of his family. All three travelled with the Guru from Anandpur Sahib and were arrested with him.
## The martyrdoms

Bhai Mati Das Ji was asked to give up his faith and refused. He was tied between two posts and sawn in two from the head down, reciting Japji Sahib as long as he could. Bhai Dyala Ji was boiled alive in a cauldron, and Bhai Sati Das Ji was wrapped in cotton soaked in oil and set alight. Each remained calm, in remembrance of the Divine, to the end. The Guru's own shaheedi followed shortly after at Chandni Chowk.
## How they are remembered

Their names are spoken in every Ardas, among those who were sawn apart and boiled alive and did not waver. The Bhai Mati Das Museum stands opposite Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Delhi, and a chowk there is named after the three. Sangats remember them with kirtan and Ardas, especially at Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, in the days before the Guru's Shaheedi Purab.

events: Shaheedi – Bhai Jivan Singh (Bhai Jaita Ji)
title: Bhai Jaita Ji (Bhai Jivan Singh): Rangrete Guru ke bete
desc: Bhai Jaita Ji carried the head of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji from Delhi to Anandpur Sahib in 1675, later became Bhai Jivan Singh, and fell at Chamkaur in 1704.
alt: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Punjab
cap: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Anandpur Sahib, where the Guru's head was cremated
body: This day remembers Bhai Jaita Ji, later Bhai Jivan Singh Ji, whose courage in 1675 gave the Sikhs one of the most moving moments in their history, and who gave his own life in the battles of December 1704.
## The head of the Guru

Bhai Jaita Ji belonged to a family of sweepers, the community the caste order held lowest, who had long served the Gurus. He was in Delhi when Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji was beheaded at Chandni Chowk in November 1675. No one dared claim the body. In the confusion of a sudden storm, Bhai Jaita Ji took up the Guru's head, wrapped it, and carried it in secret, travelling by night, all the way to Kiratpur and Anandpur Sahib. The young Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji received it, embraced him, and blessed him with the words Rangrete Guru ke bete, the Rangretas are the Guru's own sons. The head was cremated where Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Anandpur Sahib, now stands.
## Bhai Jivan Singh

Bhai Jaita Ji took Amrit at the creation of the Khalsa in 1699 and became Bhai Jivan Singh Ji. He was a skilled warrior and a poet, and served close to the Guru at Anandpur Sahib, where he is remembered as commanding Sikhs in its defence. When the Guru left Anandpur Sahib in December 1704, Bhai Jivan Singh Ji rode with him, and he fell fighting at Chamkaur Sahib, among the Singhs who held back the Mughal army.
## How he is remembered
Sikhs remember him with kirtan and Ardas, especially at Anandpur Sahib and Chamkaur Sahib, and as a reminder that the Guru's house knows no caste.

events: Saka Chamkaur Sahib
Shaheedi – Sahibzada Baba Ajit Singh Ji (Saka Chamkaur)
Shaheedi – Sahibzada Baba Jujhar Singh Ji (Saka Chamkaur)
title: Saka Chamkaur Sahib: the shaheedi of the Vadde Sahibzade, Baba Ajit Singh and Baba Jujhar Singh
name: Saka Chamkaur Sahib
desc: In December 1704, at the garhi of Chamkaur, the elder sons of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Baba Ajit Singh Ji and Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, gave their lives. The story of the saka.
alt: Gurdwara Qatalgarh Sahib at Chamkaur Sahib
cap: Gurdwara Qatalgarh Sahib, Chamkaur, where the elder Sahibzade fell
body: Saka Chamkaur Sahib remembers the battle at Chamkaur in December 1704, in which the two elder sons of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Baba Ajit Singh Ji, aged about eighteen, and Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, aged about fourteen, gave their lives with a small band of Singhs against a vast Mughal army.
## The flight from Anandpur

After a long siege, the Guru left Anandpur Sahib on promises of safe passage sworn on the Quran and on a cow. The promises were broken and the Sikhs were attacked as they crossed the flooded Sirsa river, where the Guru's family was scattered. The Guru, his two elder sons and about forty Singhs reached Chamkaur and took shelter in a mud fortress, a garhi, belonging to a local landowner. By morning they were surrounded.
## Five at a time

With only a few arrows and swords left, the Singhs went out of the garhi in groups of five to meet the besiegers. Baba Ajit Singh Ji asked his father's permission to go, and the Guru armed him himself. He fought until he fell. Seeing this, Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, still a boy, asked to follow his brother; tradition remembers the Guru embracing him and sending him out, and watching from the garhi as he too fell. Through the day the Singhs held the army back, among them three of the Panj Pyare, Bhai Mohkam Singh Ji, Bhai Himmat Singh Ji and Bhai Sahib Singh Ji.
## How the saka is remembered

Gurdwara Qatalgarh Sahib marks the place where the Sahibzade and the Singhs fell, and Gurdwara Garhi Sahib the fortress. The Shaheedi Jorh Mela at Chamkaur Sahib draws great sangats for kirtan, katha and Ardas, and many Sikh families spend these December days in simple living, sleeping on the floor and keeping from celebrations.

events: Shaheedi – Bhai Sangat Singh Ji
title: Bhai Sangat Singh Ji: the Singh who stayed at Chamkaur in the Guru's place
desc: When the Guru Khalsa asked Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji to leave the garhi of Chamkaur, Bhai Sangat Singh Ji stayed behind wearing the Guru's kalgi, and fell the next day.
body: This day remembers Bhai Sangat Singh Ji, one of the last Singhs left in the garhi of Chamkaur Sahib in December 1704. When the Guru left the besieged fortress at night, he stayed behind in the Guru's place, so that the army outside would believe the Guru was still within.
## The night at Chamkaur

By the end of the first day at Chamkaur, both elder Sahibzade and most of the Singhs had fallen, and only a handful remained in the mud fortress. Acting as the Panj Pyare, five of them asked Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji to escape so that he could continue to lead the Panth, and the Guru obeyed the Khalsa. Before he went, tradition remembers that he placed his kalgi, the plume he wore in his turban, and his dress on Bhai Sangat Singh Ji, who resembled him in height and features, and seated him in his place.
## Holding the garhi

The Guru slipped out in the darkness with three Singhs. In the morning the besiegers attacked the garhi expecting to take the Guru, and met Bhai Sangat Singh Ji and the few remaining Singhs, who fought until every one of them fell. Some accounts hold that the commanders, finding the body in the Guru's dress, believed for a time that the Guru had been killed, which gave him precious hours to get away towards the Machhiwara forest.
## How he is remembered

Many accounts give Bhai Sangat Singh Ji's earlier name as Bhai Sangtia Ji, and some link him to the family of Bhai Jaita Ji. He is remembered at Chamkaur Sahib with kirtan and Ardas during the Shaheedi Jorh Mela, and as an example of selfless sacrifice for the Guru and the Panth.

events: Shaheedi – Mata Gujri Ji
Shaheedi – Sahibzada Baba Fateh Singh Ji
Shaheedi – Sahibzada Baba Zorawar Singh Ji
title: Saka Sirhind: the shaheedi of the Chhote Sahibzade and Mata Gujri Ji
name: Shaheedi – Chhote Sahibzade and Mata Gujri Ji
desc: In December 1704 Baba Zorawar Singh Ji, 9, and Baba Fateh Singh Ji, 6, were bricked into a wall at Sirhind, and Mata Gujri Ji passed away in the Thanda Burj. The story.
cap: Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib, Sirhind, where the younger Sahibzade were martyred
body: Saka Sirhind remembers the martyrdom in December 1704 of the two youngest sons of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Baba Zorawar Singh Ji, aged nine, and Baba Fateh Singh Ji, aged six, and of their grandmother, Mata Gujri Ji. It is among the most sorrowful days in the Sikh year.
## Betrayed

When the Guru's family was scattered at the flooded Sirsa river, Mata Gujri Ji and the two youngest Sahibzade were separated from the rest. Their former cook, Gangu, offered them shelter in his village, Saheri, and then betrayed them to the authorities for a reward. They were taken to Sirhind and held in the Thanda Burj, an open tower, through bitter winter nights. Tradition remembers that Bhai Moti Ram Mehra, a servant in the governor's kitchens, risked his life to bring them milk.
## The court of Wazir Khan

The Sahibzade were brought before Wazir Khan, the governor of Sirhind, and offered wealth and safety if they would give up their faith. They refused, entering the court with a loud Fateh. Sher Mohammad Khan, the Nawab of Malerkotla, protested that children should not be punished for their father, a protest Sikhs still honour as the haa da naara. The governor ordered them to be bricked alive into a wall; when the wall collapsed, they were put to death. On hearing the news, Mata Gujri Ji passed away in the tower.
## How the day is remembered

Diwan Todar Mal, a wealthy merchant, bought the land for their cremation by covering it with gold coins. Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib marks the place, and Gurdwara Jyoti Sarup the cremation. The Shaheedi Jorh Mela at Fatehgarh Sahib draws vast sangats, and many families keep the week simply, in remembrance.

events: Shaheedi – Baba Banda Singh Bahadur Ji
title: Baba Banda Singh Bahadur: from Nanded to Sirhind and his shaheedi in Delhi
desc: Baba Banda Singh Bahadur took Sirhind in 1710, set up Sikh rule from Lohgarh and gave land to those who tilled it. His capture and his martyrdom in Delhi in June 1716.
body: This day remembers the martyrdom of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur in Delhi in June 1716. In the eight years after he met Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, he led the Khalsa to its first great victories and set up the first Sikh rule in Punjab.
## From Madho Das to Banda Singh

Born Lachhman Dev in 1670 in Rajouri, he became an ascetic called Madho Das and kept a hermitage at Nanded on the Godavari. In 1708 Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji came to Nanded; tradition remembers that Madho Das tried to overawe the Guru with his powers and failed, and fell at his feet saying he was the Guru's banda, his servant. He took Amrit as Banda Singh, and the Guru sent him to Punjab with five arrows, a nishan sahib, a drum and a council of five Singhs.
## The victories

Sikhs rallied to him across Punjab. In 1709 he took Samana, and in May 1710 he defeated Wazir Khan, the governor responsible for the death of the younger Sahibzade, at Chappar Chiri, and took Sirhind. He made Lohgarh, near Sadhaura, his capital, struck coins in the name of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Guru Gobind Singh Ji, and abolished the zamindari system, giving land to those who tilled it.
## Capture and martyrdom

In 1715 a huge Mughal army besieged him at Gurdas Nangal for eight months until the starving garrison was overrun. He was taken to Delhi in an iron cage with hundreds of Sikhs, who were executed day after day, not one accepting the offer of life for conversion. On the day, his young son Ajai Singh was killed before his eyes, and Banda Singh was tortured and put to death. Gurdwaras hold kirtan and Ardas in his memory.

events: Shaheedi Purab – Bhai Mani Singh Ji
title: Bhai Mani Singh Ji: the scribe of the Damdami Bir and his shaheedi in Lahore
desc: Bhai Mani Singh Ji wrote out Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji at Damdama Sahib and served as granthi at Amritsar. In 1738 he was cut apart joint by joint in Lahore. His story.
body: The Shaheedi Purab of Bhai Mani Singh Ji remembers the martyrdom in Lahore in 1738 of one of the most learned and devoted Sikhs of his age, who served the Gurus for most of his life and is named in every Ardas among those who were cut apart, joint by joint.
## A lifetime of service

Bhai Mani Singh Ji came to the court of Sri Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji as a child and grew up beside the young Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, becoming his close companion. He took Amrit in 1699, and many of his brothers and sons gave their lives in the battles of the Guru's time. At Damdama Sahib in 1706 he was the scribe who wrote out Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji as the Guru dictated, adding the bani of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji. After the Guru, Mata Sundari Ji sent him to Amritsar as granthi of Sri Harmandir Sahib, where he settled disputes in the Panth and preached for many years. Tradition also credits him with gathering the bani of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
## The Diwali tax

In 1738 he sought permission from Zakariya Khan, the governor of Lahore, for Sikhs to gather at Amritsar for Diwali, and agreed to pay a heavy tax from the offerings. Fearing an attack, the governor sent troops, the sangat scattered, and the tax could not be raised. Bhai Mani Singh Ji was arrested and taken to Lahore.
## The shaheedi

Offered his life if he accepted Islam, he refused. He was sentenced to be cut apart joint by joint, and when the executioner began with his wrist, tradition remembers he held out his hand at the fingers, reminding him of his orders. He bore it in calm remembrance of the Divine. Gurdwaras hold kirtan, katha and Ardas in his memory.

events: Shaheedi Purab – Bhai Taru Singh Ji
Birth anniversary – Bhai Taru Singh Ji
title: Bhai Taru Singh Ji: the young farmer who gave his scalp rather than his kes
name: Bhai Taru Singh Ji
desc: Bhai Taru Singh Ji of Poohla fed Sikhs hiding in the forests and, in 1745, chose to have his scalp removed rather than cut his kes. His life, his shaheedi, and both his days.
body: Bhai Taru Singh Ji is remembered twice in the Nanakshahi calendar, at his birth anniversary and at his Shaheedi Purab. His story, from the dark years of the eighteenth century, is the clearest example in Sikh history of devotion to the kes, the uncut hair that is part of the Sikh form.
## The farmer of Poohla

Bhai Taru Singh Ji was born in 1720 at Poohla, a village near Amritsar, and lived with his widowed mother and his sister. In those years the governors of Lahore had put a price on the head of every Sikh, and many Singhs lived in the forests and deserts. Bhai Taru Singh Ji farmed his land and quietly shared what he grew with them, giving them food and shelter.
## Arrest

In 1745 an informer, Harbhagat Niranjania, reported him to Zakariya Khan, the governor of Lahore, for helping the rebels. He was arrested and brought to Lahore. The governor offered him his life if he would accept Islam and cut his hair. He refused. Tradition remembers that when told his kes would be cut, he answered that his hair would go with his scalp, and asked for no other mercy.
## The shaheedi

On the governor's orders his scalp was removed with a sharp blade. He bore it calmly, reciting the bani. He lived on for some days, and tradition holds that Zakariya Khan fell ill and died before him. Gurdwara Shaheed Bhai Taru Singh Ji in Lahore marks the place.
## How he is remembered
Sikhs remember him with kirtan, katha and Ardas on both days. Many gurdwaras use the occasion to speak about the kes and the dastar, and young Sikhs often hold turban-tying camps in his memory.

events: Shaheedi Purab – Baba Deep Singh Ji
Birth anniversary – Baba Deep Singh Ji
title: Baba Deep Singh Ji: the scholar-warrior who fought his way to Amritsar
name: Baba Deep Singh Ji
desc: Baba Deep Singh Ji copied Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji at Damdama Sahib, led the Shaheedan Misl, and in 1757, aged 75, fell fighting to free Sri Harmandir Sahib. His two days.
alt: Gurdwara Shaheed Baba Deep Singh Ji in Amritsar
cap: Gurdwara Shaheed Baba Deep Singh Ji, Amritsar, at the place where he fell
body: Baba Deep Singh Ji is remembered twice in the Nanakshahi calendar, at his birth anniversary in winter and at his Shaheedi Purab in autumn. He was both a scholar of the Guru's bani and one of the bravest warriors of the eighteenth century.
## Scholar of Damdama Sahib

Born in 1682 at Pahuwind, near Amritsar, Deep Singh Ji came to Anandpur Sahib as a young man and took Amrit from Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji. He learned Gurmukhi and the bani there, and stayed at Damdama Sahib with Bhai Mani Singh Ji while Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji was written out. He later made several handwritten copies of the scripture, sent to the Takhts, and taught at the centre of learning that grew at Damdama Sahib, remembered as the Guru Ki Kashi.
## The Shaheedan Misl

In the 1730s, when the Khalsa was organised into misls, Baba Deep Singh Ji led the Shaheedan Misl, its members sworn to give their lives for the Panth. He fought alongside Banda Singh Bahadur and in many later battles.
## The last battle

In 1757 Ahmad Shah Abdali's forces, under Jahan Khan, desecrated Sri Harmandir Sahib and filled its sarovar with debris. Baba Deep Singh Ji, then seventy-five, vowed to celebrate Diwali at Amritsar. He drew a line in the earth, asked those ready to die to cross it, and set out, thousands joining him on the way. Near Amritsar, at Gohalwar, he was gravely wounded. Sikh tradition remembers that, holding his head on his palm, he fought on to reach the sacred precincts. Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Baba Deep Singh Ji marks the place, and sangats gather there for kirtan and Ardas on both days.

events: Shaheedi – Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji
title: Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji: thirty Singhs against Abdali at Sri Harmandir Sahib
desc: In December 1764 Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji and about thirty Singhs stayed at Amritsar to defend Sri Harmandir Sahib against Ahmad Shah Abdali's army and fell to the last man.
alt: Gurdwara Shaheed Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji, Amritsar
cap: Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji, behind Sri Akal Takht Sahib
body: This day remembers Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji and about thirty Singhs who stayed at Amritsar in December 1764 to defend Sri Harmandir Sahib against the army of Ahmad Shah Abdali, knowing they could not win, and fell to the last man.
## A Nihang of the Shaheedan Misl

Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji was born in 1688 at Lil, near Khem Karan, and is remembered as having taken Amrit as a young man, by many accounts from Bhai Mani Singh Ji. He spent his life in the service of the Panth and of Sri Harmandir Sahib, and was a Nihang of the Shaheedan Misl, the band once led by Baba Deep Singh Ji.
## The seventh invasion

In the winter of 1764 Ahmad Shah Abdali crossed into Punjab on his seventh invasion and marched on Amritsar. Most of the Khalsa forces were away, and the Sikhs in the city were few. Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji, then in his seventies, chose to stay and defend the Guru's house. He and about thirty companions prepared themselves, did Ardas, and waited at the complex as the invading army approached.
## The last stand

When the army of thousands reached the precincts, the Singhs came out to meet it at the gates and fought until every one of them fell. The Persian chronicler Qazi Nur Muhammad, who travelled with Abdali's army, wrote of the few Sikhs who came out to face it, with no fear of death. Abdali's forces then demolished Sri Harmandir Sahib, which the Khalsa rebuilt soon after.
## How the day is remembered
Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Baba Gurbakhsh Singh Ji, behind Sri Akal Takht Sahib, marks the place where they were cremated, and sangats remember them there with kirtan and Ardas.

events: Wadda Ghallughara – Kup Rohira, Sangrur
Annual Jorh Mela remembering Wadda Ghallughara – Gahil, Barnala (supplementary cross-check)
title: Wadda Ghallughara 1762: the great massacre at Kup Rohira
name: Wadda Ghallughara – Kup Rohira
desc: In February 1762 Ahmad Shah Abdali's forces caught a Sikh caravan near Kup Rohira, and tens of thousands were killed in a day. The story, and the Jorh Melas that remember it.
body: The Wadda Ghallughara, the great holocaust, took place on 5 February 1762 near the villages of Kup and Rohira, in today's Malerkotla district. In a single day the forces of Ahmad Shah Abdali killed a very large number of Sikhs, many of them women, children and the elderly. Sikh sources speak of tens of thousands; historians usually give figures between ten and thirty thousand. It is remembered as one of the darkest days in Sikh history.
## The caravan

Early in 1762 the Sikhs were moving their families south from the Majha to the safety of the Malwa desert, near Barnala. Abdali, on his sixth invasion, made a forced march from Lahore with his army and joined the forces of the governor of Sirhind and the Nawab of Malerkotla, surprising the camp at Kup before dawn.
## A moving wall

The Khalsa, led by Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and Charat Singh Sukerchakia, formed a ring around the caravan of non-combatants and fought as they marched, mile after mile, through the whole day. Jassa Singh Ahluwalia was wounded many times. By evening, near Gahil and Kutba-Bahmania, the survivors reached water and the attackers fell back. Abdali went on to blow up Sri Harmandir Sahib. Yet within months the Khalsa had regrouped and defeated his forces, and within two years they ruled Sirhind.
## How it is remembered

The day is observed with Akhand Paath, kirtan and Ardas. Sangats gather at the memorial at Kup Rohira, built at the site of the massacre, and at Gahil in Barnala district, where an annual Jorh Mela remembers the end of that day's march.
